name: Jabin
overview: Jabin was a male king who reigned over Hazor, a significant city in Canaan, during the period of Israel's conquest under Joshua. He is notably recognized as one of the thirty-one kings defeated by Joshua, highlighting his role as a leader opposing Israel's settlement. Scripture identifies him specifically as the King of Hazor and King of Canaan, marking him as a prominent figure among the Canaanite rulers.
namesAndTitles: The name Jabin means 'perceptive,' reflecting a proper name of Hebrew origin. His titles, 'King of Hazor' and 'King of Canaan,' indicate his royal authority over the city of Hazor and his broader rule among the Canaanite peoples. None of these names or titles are described as given directly by God.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records a relationship between Jabin and Sisera, indicating that Jabin was king over Sisera, who served under him. Beyond this, the biblical text does not provide further family relationships or lineage for Jabin.
scriptureSignificance: Jabin's significance lies in his opposition to the Israelites during their divinely sanctioned conquest of Canaan. As the King of Hazor, he led a coalition of Canaanite kings against Joshua and Israel but was ultimately defeated, demonstrating God's power in establishing Israel in the Promised Land. His defeat marks a pivotal moment in the fulfillment of God's promise to give the land to His people.
